name: Cloud-360 GCP Well-Architected MVP Lens
description: Offline Custom Lens for GCP architecture diagrams, aligned with Google Cloud Well-Architected Framework pillars (Operational excellence; Security, privacy, and compliance; Reliability; Cost optimization; Performance optimization). Sustainability is noted in Framework but not scored as a sixth pillar here (Cloud-360 keeps five WA-compatible pillar ids). Adapted for diagram review—not a live GCP audit. Reference: https://docs.cloud.google.com/architecture/framework

questions.title: [GCAF] How do you protect public ingress (security by design / zero trust edge)?
questions.description: Google Cloud Well-Architected Framework (Security) emphasizes security by design and zero trust. Look for Cloud Armor, external HTTP(S) Load Balancing, Cloud CDN, API Gateway, or Identity-Aware Proxy at the edge.

choices.title: Cloud Armor / HTTPS LB / IAP edge is present

improvementPlan.displayText: Put Cloud Armor in front of external HTTP(S) Load Balancing; consider IAP for admin/internal apps (GCAF Security: zero trust / edge protection).
Terminate TLS at the load balancer (Google-managed or Certificate Manager) and enforce HTTPS.

questions.title: [GCAF] How are secrets and data at rest protected?
questions.description: Look for Cloud KMS / CMEK, Secret Manager, private VPC, Private Google Access, or Private Service Connect on data planes.

choices.title: Cloud KMS / CMEK / Secret Manager is labeled

improvementPlan.displayText: Use Cloud KMS (CMEK) and Secret Manager for keys/secrets on Cloud Storage, Cloud SQL, Spanner, and similar services.

choices.title: Private networking for data is labeled

improvementPlan.displayText: Keep databases private; use Private Google Access / PSC; avoid public data endpoints (GCAF Security).

questions.title: [GCAF] How do you build high availability through redundancy?
questions.description: GCAF Reliability: build HA through redundancy and regional / multi-zone design. Look for multiple zones, regional MIG, Cloud SQL HA, Spanner multi-region.

choices.title: Multiple zones / regional resources are shown

improvementPlan.displayText: Deploy critical tiers across at least two zones (regional MIG / multi-zone) per GCAF Reliability redundancy guidance.

choices.title: DB HA / replica / failover is labeled

improvementPlan.displayText: Enable Cloud SQL HA or Spanner multi-region and label failover paths.

questions.title: [GCAF] Do you take advantage of horizontal scalability?
questions.description: GCAF Reliability: horizontal scalability. Look for Managed Instance Groups, autoscaling, GKE HPA/VPA, Cloud Run scaling, or load-balanced replicas.

choices.title: MIG / autoscaling / horizontal scale is labeled

improvementPlan.displayText: Use regional MIGs, GKE autoscaling, or Cloud Run concurrency/scaling so capacity grows with load.

questions.title: [GCAF] How do you plan recovery / multi-regional resilience?
questions.description: GCAF Reliability covers recovery testing and realistic targets. Look for multi-region Spanner, cross-region replicas, backup, or DR labels.

improvementPlan.displayText: For critical data, design multi-regional or cross-region failover and document RPO/RTO.
Enable backups (Cloud SQL / GCS) and show restore testing in the architecture narrative.

questions.title: [GCAF] How do you optimize resource / storage usage?
questions.description: GCAF Cost optimization: optimize resource usage continuously. Look for storage classes (Nearline/Coldline/Archive), lifecycle rules, CUD, Spot/preemptible, or rightsizing labels.

choices.title: Lifecycle / class / CUD / Spot optimization is labeled

improvementPlan.displayText: Add Cloud Storage lifecycle policies or appropriate classes; for compute, evaluate CUD, Spot VM, and autoscaling (GCAF Cost).

questions.title: [GCAF] How do you plan allocation and accelerate hot paths?
questions.description: GCAF Performance optimization: plan resource allocation and improve continuously. Look for Memorystore, Cloud CDN, global LB, or caching tiers.

choices.title: Memorystore / Cloud CDN / cache tier is present

improvementPlan.displayText: Add Memorystore (Redis) and/or Cloud CDN for latency-sensitive reads; size tiers to demand.

questions.title: [GCAF] How do you operate with CloudOps observability and change automation?
questions.description: GCAF Operational excellence: CloudOps readiness, incident management, automate change. Look for Cloud Monitoring, Logging, Error Reporting, alerting, and CI/CD (Cloud Build / Deploy).

improvementPlan.displayText: Add Cloud Monitoring metrics/logs, dashboards, and SLOs for user-experience reliability goals.
Create alerting policies with notification channels for incident response (GCAF Ops).
